title: Indian Box Office Surges as Hollywood Blockbusters and Bollywood Hits Fill Theaters Simultaneously
excerpt: Spider-Man, The Odyssey, and Awarapan 2 are driving a rare multi-front box office boom in India, boosting PVR INOX's financials and signaling a structural recovery in theatrical exhibition.
body:
• India's box office is experiencing a rare simultaneous surge from Hollywood and Bollywood, with Spider-Man: Brand New Day crossing Rs. 320 crore, The Odyssey collecting Rs. 178 crore, and Awarapan 2 earning Rs. 92 crore in its first four days.
  • PVR INOX, India's largest multiplex chain, swung from a Rs. 545 million loss to a Rs. 565 million profit in Q1 2026, with ticket sales up 15.9% and food-and-beverage revenue climbing 16.7%.
  • The Odyssey became the highest-grossing IMAX release in Indian history, with IMAX contributing Rs. 74 crore of its Rs. 167 crore haul — a sign of growing premium-format demand.
  • Emraan Hashmi's Awarapan 2 marks his biggest solo hit in 14 years, crossing Rs. 130 crore worldwide in four days and already surpassing the lifetime collection of Raaz 3.

Indian movie theaters haven't had it this good in years. Three films — two from Hollywood, one from Bollywood — are running simultaneously in packed auditoriums across the country, delivering the kind of multi-front box office boom that seemed improbable just 18 months ago.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day has dominated since its July 30 release, crossing Rs. 320 crore in India alone. Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, despite being in its fourth week, continues to hold screens with Rs. 178 crore across all languages. And Awarapan 2, Emraan Hashmi's gritty sequel, opened on Independence Day weekend to Rs. 92 crore in its first four days.

Awarapan 2: Hashmi's Career-Defining Comeback

The numbers for Awarapan 2 carry particular weight. The film opened to Rs. 21.89 crore on Friday, August 14, surged to Rs. 33.77 crore on Independence Day Saturday, and held at Rs. 25.84 crore on Sunday before a typical Monday drop to Rs. 9.07 crore. Its worldwide gross has climbed past Rs. 130 crore.

For Hashmi, these are career-redefining figures. It has been 14 years since he delivered a solo hit of this scale, and it is fitting that his comeback vehicle is a sequel — the original Awarapan, released in 2007, flopped at the box office but became a cult classic on home video.

"The industry delivered broad-based growth, our operating metrics improved across the board, and the company is now net cash positive."

— Ajay Bijli, Managing Director, PVR INOX

Directed by Nitin Kakkar and featuring Disha Patani alongside Hashmi, Awarapan 2 is driving volume particularly in single screens and Tier 2 cities, where occupancy has outpaced multiplex chains.

Hollywood's IMAX Takeover

The Odyssey has rewritten India's premium-format playbook. In 24 days, the Christopher Nolan epic collected Rs. 166.89 crore in English alone, with IMAX contributing a staggering Rs. 74.21 crore — making it the highest-grossing IMAX release in Indian history.

Even after Spider-Man's arrival on its 14th day, The Odyssey held remarkably steady. Its Week 3 collection of Rs. 24.15 crore represented only a 47% drop from Week 2, a resilience that exhibitors attribute to repeat IMAX viewership.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day has been India's biggest pan-India Hollywood success story. Its six-day gross crossed Rs. 368 crore, with 3D screenings powering 77% of business. English-language shows generated Rs. 203 crore, Hindi-dubbed prints added Rs. 126 crore, and regional-language versions contributed another Rs. 38 crore.

PVR INOX Rides the Wave

India's largest multiplex operator is a direct beneficiary. PVR INOX reported a consolidated net profit of Rs. 565 million for the quarter ended June 30 — a dramatic swing from a Rs. 545 million loss in the same period last year, according to Reuters.

Revenue from operations climbed 11.9% year-on-year to Rs. 16.22 billion. Ticket sales rose 15.9% to Rs. 8.37 billion, while food-and-beverage spending jumped 16.7% to Rs. 5.58 billion — a sign that audiences are not just showing up but spending more once inside the theater.

The company also launched its Smart Cinema format aimed at India's smaller towns, with tickets priced 30-35% below standard multiplexes and reduced construction costs of Rs. 1.9 crore per screen compared to Rs. 3-4 crore for conventional cinemas.

Structural Recovery or Summer Spike?

The broader question is whether this momentum represents a lasting shift. India's box office grew 20% during PVR INOX's Q1, driven by a steady flow of content across Hindi, regional, and Hollywood films. But the exhibition sector has cycled through boom-and-bust phases before, often tied to the presence or absence of a few tentpole releases.

What's different this time is the breadth. The current surge isn't riding a single blockbuster — it's powered by simultaneous success across languages, genres, and formats. If that pattern holds through the festive season, India's theatrical exhibition sector may finally be emerging from the post-pandemic shadow that has hung over it since 2020.
